# mulib-project-migrate

<!-- Generated by tools/joltfx_inventory.py; edit CONTRACTS or section-7 scope, then --write-docs. -->

**Area:** Project  
**Implementation:** C11 `static inline`; no implementation switch or external ABI export  
**Status:** bounded review candidate; **not safe On1x admitted**

## Purpose and limits

Ordered monotonic schema migration execution with ambiguity rejection.

Each step must be transactional; earlier successful steps remain committed.

Retain existing upstream functionality and platform providers; this header is not a replacement for a complete media/editor/rendering stack.

## Units, ownership and capacities

s has n migration steps; version is mutable schema version and target an increasing goal. Each callback must be transactional; prior successful steps remain committed.

Byte spans and journal offsets/capacities count bytes; history/migration arrays count commands/steps. Providers and callback contexts are borrowed. Trusted callbacks must define transactions, lifetime and thread affinity. These helpers do not establish durable filesystem storage or safe archive extraction.

Capacities describe live backing storage supplied by the caller, not merely numeric metadata. Check return values before using outputs. A false result is not a universal no-mutation guarantee; low-level value helpers and bool miss/error results require the documented preconditions. Bound untrusted counts and work before calling.

## Current callable surface

Signatures extracted from this header; dependency types and complete checks are in [the source](../include/mulib-project-migrate.h). Helpers listed here are not automatically safe foreign imports.

```c
static inline bool mulib_project_migrate(const mulib_project_migrate_step *s,size_t n,uint32_t *version,uint32_t target,void *ctx);
```

## Additional source contracts

- Validate the entire unambiguous route before invoking any callback. A failed callback must roll back its own step; earlier successful steps stay committed. Callbacks must not mutate s/version or reenter this migration.

## Validation and integration

The [shared CPU example](../examples/joltfx-pipeline.c) illustrates a small image/audio/timebase slice; it does **not** exercise every API in this header. The [integration oracles](../tests/joltfx-integration-test.c) and [parser boundary probes](../tests/joltfx-parser-boundary-test.c) are representative regressions, not exhaustive coverage.

```sh
python3 tools/check_joltfx.py
```

The runner checks the 193 original kernels plus the shared PCM helper, isolated and in aggregate C11 builds with GCC/Clang, including canonical-header composition, separate-TU wrappers, an expected missing-static-inline-export link failure, a no-`__int128` path, and ASan/UBSan regressions. It does not validate native GPU/codec/audio execution, real-world compatibility, C++ or On1x ownership/admission. Explicit foreign wrappers, independent safety review and platform integration are still required.
